guide.title: The Science of 4-4-4-4 Box Breathing
guide.subtitle: Used by US Navy SEALs, peak performance athletes, and healthcare professionals to dissolve acute stress and restore razor-sharp mental clarity.
guide.whatIsText: Box breathing, also known as four-square breathing, is an autonomic regulation technique. It equalizes the four breath intervals: 4 seconds inhaling, 4 seconds holding full, 4 seconds exhaling, and 4 seconds holding empty. By tracing a balanced geometric square, you consciously override your body's fight-or-flight survival response.
guide.sealUsageHeading: Why Navy SEALs Use Square Breathing
guide.sealUsageText: During high-stress tactical operations, adrenaline surges cause rapid, shallow breathing, spiked heart rate, and severe cognitive tunnel vision. Navy SEALs practice box breathing before and during missions to stimulate the vagus nerve, lower resting heart rate, and re-engage the prefrontal cortex for calm, decisive decision-making.
guide.stepsHeading: How to Practice in 4 Simple Steps
guide.step1Desc: Draw air inward through your nose into the depths of your belly. Feel your diaphragm expand.
guide.step2Desc: Keep your lungs comfortably full without straining or clamping down on your vocal cords.
guide.step3Desc: Gently expel all air through your nose or lips, consciously relaxing your neck, jaw, and chest.
guide.step4Desc: Pause peacefully at the bottom of the breath before initiating your next inhalation.
guide.b1Desc: Triggers the parasympathetic 'rest-and-digest' state within 2 to 3 minutes, counteracting cortisol.
guide.b2Desc: Diaphragmatic expansion stimulates the vagus nerve, boosting Heart Rate Variability (HRV).
guide.b3Desc: Normalizes CO2 and O2 blood gas exchange, eliminating mental fog and fatigue under pressure.
guide.b4Desc: Rhythmic square pacing slows cardiovascular strain and helps decrease resting systolic pressure.

faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions regarding box breathing, pacing techniques, and how to get the most from this tool.

items.q: What is the 4-4-4-4 box breathing technique?
items.a: Box breathing (or square breathing) is a breath regulation method where you inhale for 4 seconds, hold your breath for 4 seconds, exhale for 4 seconds, and hold empty for 4 seconds. Visualizing the four equal sides of a square helps maintain steady pacing.

items.q: How long should I practice box breathing?
items.a: Just 2 to 5 minutes (around 8 to 20 full cycles) is sufficient to shift your nervous system out of high alert into calm focus. Many users enjoy doing 5 minutes every morning or before stressful tasks like presentations and exams.

items.q: Which box duration should I choose (3s, 4s, 5s, 6s)?
items.a: 4 seconds is the gold standard used by Navy SEALs. Beginners or individuals feeling short of breath can start with 3 seconds. For deeper meditation, 5 or 6 seconds offers a more profound down-regulation.

items.q: How does the synthesized audio cue work?
items.a: BoxBreathe uses the browser's native Web Audio API to synthesize zen singing bowl harmonic sine waves in real-time. There are zero external MP3 files to download, ensuring zero latency and 100% offline functionality.

items.q: Can box breathing help with panic attacks or insomnia?
items.a: Yes. Controlled slow breathing interrupts hyperventilation loops, signals safety to the amygdala, and lowers sympathetic tone, making it highly effective for calming panic sensations and preparing the body for deep sleep.

items.q: Is any of my personal data tracked or stored on a server?
items.a: Never. BoxBreathe is 100% client-side with zero tracking, zero cookies, zero analytics scripts, and zero server dependencies. Your completed mindful minutes are saved only in your browser's private LocalStorage.
